e.etymology: From Kunta Kinte, the Mandinka ancestor at the center of Alex Haley's Roots. Boys were given the name in 1977, the year the television miniseries aired.

assoc.t: Kunta Kinte, the hero of Alex Haley's Roots

e.etymology: A spelling of Hyman, the English form that Jewish immigrants gave to Chaim, Hebrew for life.
e.note: Hymen is an anatomical term, a main reason the name dropped out of use.

assoc.t: hymen, the membrane at the opening of the vagina

e.etymology: A spelling of Les, the short form of Leslie, a Scottish place name and surname, and of Lester, from the English city of Leicester.
The surname Council or Councill, used as a given name in the American South.
e.note: Identical to the ordinary word council.

e.etymology: A variant of Lavinia, in Roman legend the daughter of King Latinus who marries Aeneas. The name is tied to the ancient town of Lavinium and its meaning is unknown.
The family name of Kunta Kinte, the Mandinka ancestor in Alex Haley's Roots. Boys were given it in 1977, the year the television miniseries aired.

assoc.t: Kunta Kinte, the hero of Alex Haley's Roots

e.etymology: A Japanese boys' name whose meaning depends on the kanji; tatsu may be written as accomplished or as dragon, joined with o, man or husband.
A spelling of Hjalmar, from Old Norse hjalmr, helmet, and a word for army or warrior. Scandinavian immigrants brought it to the upper Midwest.

A Cantonese spelling of two common Chinese family names, the ones written Wang, king, and Huang, yellow, in Mandarin. In 1880s American records it is most likely a family name set down in the given-name position.
e.note: Overwhelmingly a Chinese family name, not a given name.

e.etymology: A romanized Chinese family name, often the Taishanese form of Chen. In 1880s American records it is most likely a family name set down in the given-name position.
e.note: Mainly a Chinese family name, and identical to the English word chin.

e.etymology: A Japanese boys' name written many ways; ji often marks a second son, and sho may be bright, correct or other characters. Shoji is also the word for a sliding paper screen, written differently.
The French form of Latin Delphinus, of Delphi, a word that also means dolphin. Saint Delphinus was a 4th-century bishop of Bordeaux; Delphine is the feminine form.
The German surname Göbel, from a medieval pet form of Godebert and similar names. Its use as a US first name peaked in 1900, the year Kentucky governor William Goebel was assassinated.
e.note: Looks and sounds close to Goebbels, the surname of Nazi propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels.

e.etymology: The surname of Marshal Ferdinand Foch, the French general who commanded the Allied armies in 1918. American parents gave it as a first name that year in his honor.
namesakes: Ferdinand Foch (French marshal who led the Allied armies in World War I)
